reasons: Read only. The tests were not run during this reading.
The tests cover validation, labels, editor text and request shapes.

terms.meaning: Where a value came from, such as measured source data, a typical assumption, or a manual edit.
A saved description of one part in an assembly: its shape, size, position, rotation, material and how many times it repeats.
Sample data prepared in advance for a test to use.
A fake stand-in for the real server that returns set answers during tests.
A version number sent with each change so the server can refuse a change made to an old copy.

used_by: No app file imports it. It is run directly by the test runner.

sections.name: File setup, typical
sections.title: Test setup and shared sample data
sections.what: Imports the test tools and the code under test, then prepares a sample typical provenance label and a new empty recipe named tank.
sections.why: Likely reason: the other tests reuse these samples, so they are prepared once at the top.

sections.name: part
sections.title: Sample explicit part
sections.what: Builds a sample part from the recipe with typical provenance on every value and no source links. It stands in for a part that came from the model without any evidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: tests need a part with no evidence attached to check that its values are labelled as unverified.
sections.watch_out: Because it has no source links, any test that uses it treats its values as unverified.

sections.name: assembly recipes and provenance (part 1)
sections.title: Tests for starting recipes and validation
sections.what: Checks that a stored recipe is used first, then explicit parts, then a single default box. Also checks that degree input becomes radians, that identity and evidence are not sent, that invalid numbers, unequal cylinder diameters, duplicate slots and too many parts are refused, and that the labels follow the evidence rules.
sections.why: Likely reason: these checks keep the editor's starting point and saved data predictable and make sure bad input never reaches the server.
sections.watch_out: The validation tests pin exact limits such as 256 recipes, 4,096 expanded parts and 100,000 m, so changing a limit means changing these tests.

sections.name: assembly recipes and provenance (part 2)
sections.title: Tests for label rules and editor text
sections.what: Checks that repeats accepted by the user are labelled manual, that count-one defaults stay unverified, and that the editor page shows the required disclosures, the phase scope note, the empty template library and the material choices with the unknown-key note.
sections.why: Likely reason: the labels tell users which values are trustworthy, and the disclosures keep the editor from implying a precise starting shape.
sections.watch_out: The tests look for exact wording in the disclosures, so rewording them will fail the tests even when the meaning is unchanged.

sections.name: assembly API wire contract
sections.title: Tests for the save request shapes
sections.what: Checks that saving an assembly, saving a template, updating a template, assigning a template and deleting a template each send the right address, method and body, with the revision number and encoded names. Also checks that a stale-revision conflict is returned once with no retry.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server only accepts requests in exactly this shape, and a conflict must reach the user rather than being hidden by a retry.
sections.watch_out: Some checks compare the body as exact text, so changing the order of fields in a request breaks the test even when the data is the same.

summary: Tests that check how the assembly editor builds, labels and saves its part recipes.
purpose: Confirm the assembly feature keeps its rules: valid recipes, correct labels for where each value came from, the editor's required warnings, and exact request shapes sent to the server.
why: Likely reason: the assembly code has many edge cases such as limits, unit conversions and labels, so tests hold the expected behaviour in place. Reason for the specific test values is not stated in the code.
how: 1. Prepare sample data (a typical part, a new recipe, a test component). 2. Check the starting recipes and the fallback box. 3. Check conversion from degree input to radians and that part identity is not sent. 4. Check the validation limits and error messages. 5. Check the provenance labels for manual, evidence and default values. 6. Render the editor and check its required wording. 7. Check the request addresses, bodies and the single conflict response.
inputs: No outside input. It uses sample data written in the file and fake server responses.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test when the test runner runs the file. Nothing is produced in the app.
risks: Tests check exact wording and exact request text, so harmless edits to wording or key order will make them fail.
debug: If a test fails, compare the expected text with the component it names. If validation tests fail, check the limits in assembly.ts. If request tests fail, compare the key order in the expected body with the code that builds it.
